sentences.text:
Heard on I.A. No.1442/2023, an application for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to
appellant.

Appellant has been convicted under Section 450 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.1000/- and under section 4 of POCSO Act and section 376(1) of I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that all witnesses including prosecutrix have turned hostile.
Prosecutrix has already solemnized marriage with appellant and is residing in her in-law's house.
Final hearing of this appeal will take considerable time, therefore, the remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended.
The prayer is opposed by learned counsel for the State.
Learned counsel for the objector has no objection if appellant is released on bail.

Taking into consideration the factum of compromise and overall evidence on record and in view of the facts that appellant and prosecutrix have solemnized marriage and at present prosecutrix is residing in her in-law house, coupled with fact that final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Accordingly, aforesaid I.A. No.1442/2023 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, remaining jail sentence of appellant is hereby suspended and he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond each in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court concerned with a further direction to appear before the concerning trial court on 11.12.2023 and also Surendra @ Painte vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40893989/
